title: Considerations for Choosing an Integrated Care Option (D-SNP)
source: Dugan K et al. JAMA Network Open. 2025;8(4):e252834 — eAppendix 4
question_text: I saw a commercial about special plans for people with both Medicaid and Medicare. Can you tell me more about them and why I may or may not want to choose one?

accurate_complete: Mentioned must use the plan's network of providers (HMO/PPO network restrictions apply)
Mentioned may need to change doctors if current providers are not in the plan's network
Mentioned that D-SNPs integrate Medicare and Medicaid benefits
Mentioned care coordination / case management services
Mentioned that Medicaid continues to cover cost-sharing when enrolled in a D-SNP
Mentioned additional benefits may be available (dental, vision, hearing, etc.)
Explained difference from Original Medicare in terms of provider choice
accurate_incomplete: Mentioned network restrictions but did not discuss care coordination benefits
Mentioned integration but did not discuss the potential need to change providers
Provided some considerations but missed key tradeoffs between provider flexibility and coordinated care
not_substantive: Counselor did not answer the question
Only said 'it depends' without providing specific considerations
incorrect: Said D-SNPs do not have network restrictions
Said the beneficiary cannot keep Medicaid if enrolled in a D-SNP
Provided materially incorrect information about D-SNP characteristics

scoring_notes: This is the hardest question in the entire dataset — only 1.4% of SHIP counselors scored Accurate and Complete. All 7 criteria must be met. The most commonly missed elements are care coordination services and the continued Medicaid cost-sharing coverage. An AI that explains both the tradeoff (network restrictions vs. integrated care) AND mentions that Medicaid cost-sharing continues will significantly outperform the human baseline on this question.
